title: Incidents
subtitle: Track and manage monitoring incidents
noIncidentsForCheck: No incidents found for this check
flappingHint: Opened at flap level {{count}} — adaptive recovery escalated the required stability before this incident's auto-resolve.

snoozeDialog.title: Snooze incident
snoozeDialog.description: Silence notifications until the chosen time. Snoozing also acknowledges the incident.

failureDetails.title: First failure
failureDetails.description: Snapshot of the result that triggered this incident — captured before raw results age out of retention.

probeResponse.title: What the probe saw
probeResponse.description: The response this check received when the incident opened — one probe, one region, one instant. It is evidence of the failure, not the target's current state.
probeResponse.redactionNote: Response headers only. Sensitive values (cookies, authorization, tokens, keys, secrets) are redacted, and the check's own request headers are never captured.
probeResponse.binary: Body not stored: it is binary or not valid UTF-8. Metadata only — {{size}}, SHA-256 {{hash}}.

screenshot.title: Screenshot at failure detection
screenshot.description: What the page looked like when this check reported the failure. Captured a moment AFTER detection, from one region — treat it as evidence, not as the failing frame itself.
screenshot.alt: Screenshot of the page captured when the incident opened
screenshot.caption: Captured {{capturedAt}} from {{region}}, shortly after failure detection.

traceroute.title: Network path at failure
traceroute.description: An MTR-style traceroute taken right after this incident opened, from the probing region toward the address the failing check dialed.
traceroute.loadFailed: The path capture could not be loaded. Its download link is short-lived — reload the incident to sign a fresh one.
traceroute.tcpModeNotice: This host could not open an ICMP socket, so the path was probed with plain TCP connects. That measures how far the packets got, but it cannot show which routers are in between — a blank hop here means "not observable", not "no reply".
traceroute.truncated: The time budget ran out before the trace reached the target. What is shown is real, but it is not the whole path.
traceroute.incomplete: The trace never reached the target. The last hop that answered is where the path stops working.
traceroute.caption: Captured at {{startedAt}}, in {{durationMs}} ms — after the failing probe was already reported, so it never delayed the incident.

comments.title: Comments
comments.description: Notes from responders and Slack thread replies.
comments.empty: No comments yet. Add the first note below.

rollup.causedByActive: Rolled up under {{parent}} incident — paging is suppressed while the root cause is open.
rollup.causedByPast: This incident was rolled up under {{parent}} until {{resolvedAt}}. Paging fired then.
rollup.blastRadiusFooter: Paging will fire on any child still down when this incident resolves.
rollup.blastRadiusEmpty: No child incidents currently rolled up under this one.

statusUpdatesCard.title: Status updates
statusUpdatesCard.description: Narrative updates published to your status page for this incident.
statusUpdatesCard.empty: No status updates yet for this incident.

dialog.linkedDescription: This update will be linked to this incident on the status page.
dialog.deleteConfirmDescription: This will remove the update from the status page.

notificationsCard.title: Notifications
notificationsCard.description: Who was notified and the delivery status.
notificationsCard.empty: No notifications recorded for this incident yet.

publications.description: Status pages where customers can see this incident. Publishing writes a customer-readable title — never the internal one.
publications.notPublished: Not published on any status page.
publications.unpublishDescription: It disappears from the public status page immediately. The publication and its updates are kept for audit, and the incident can be published again later.
publications.autopilotDescription: It was published automatically and will resolve itself when the underlying incident recovers. The moment you edit it or post an update, it becomes yours — the automation will then only report the recovery and leave the final resolve to you.
publications.publicDetailsDescription: Everything here is shown to customers. Never paste probe output, error strings, internal hostnames or IP addresses into it.
publications.postUpdateDescription: Updates are append-only: there is no edit and no delete. Choosing investigating, identified, monitoring or resolved also moves the incident to that state.
publications.updateBodyPlaceholder: We have identified the cause and are deploying a fix.
publications.noAffected: No affected components resolved for this page.
